pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae Ia q.22 a.1
pairs.question: Utrum providentia Deo conveniat?
pairs.answer: Necesse est ponere providentiam in Deo.
pairs.derivation: Question is the article 1 title (interrogative 'utrum' quaestio), also posed at line 18 'Primo: utrum Deo conveniat providentia'. Answer is the operative first sentence of the Respondeo (line 39), dropping the framing tag 'Respondeo dicendum quod'; it ends at the first full stop. What follows ('Omne enim bonum quod est in rebus...') is the supporting argument/elaboration, not part of the direct answer.

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae Ia q.22 a.2
pairs.question: Utrum omnia sint subiecta divinae providentiae?
pairs.answer: Necesse est dicere omnia divinae providentiae subiacere, non in universali tantum, sed etiam in singulari.
pairs.derivation: Question is the article 2 title. The Respondeo (line 65) opens with a non-answering preamble surveying others' positions ('quidam totaliter providentiam negaverunt, sicut Democritus et Epicurei... aliorum opinionem est secutus'), which does not answer; per the skip-preamble rule I advance the answer's start to the operative answering sentence, dropping its leading 'Sed' which merely contrasts with the surveyed opinions. Answer ends at the first full stop; what follows ('Quod sic patet. Cum enim omne agens...') is the demonstration.

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae Ia q.22 a.4
pairs.question: Utrum providentia rebus provisis necessitatem imponat?
pairs.answer: Providentia divina quibusdam rebus necessitatem imponit, non autem omnibus, ut quidam crediderunt.
pairs.derivation: Question is the article 4 title. Answer is the operative first sentence of the Respondeo (line 113), dropping the framing 'Respondeo dicendum quod'; it directly and fully answers (necessity on some things, not all). Ends at the first full stop; what follows ('Ad providentiam enim pertinet ordinare res in finem...') is the supporting reasoning.
